source_refs.note: 2- Identifying Drug Targets: a main subheading of 7.1 Applications of structural biology, its own page (owner 2026-11-04); PDF 171-171.

blocks.text: Structural biology helps scientists find the right place on a disease-causing molecule where a drug can work. These places are usually proteins and are called drug targets. By studying the 3D shape of these proteins, scientists can find specific spots where a drug can attach and stop the protein from working. For example, in COVID-19, scientists used structural biology to study the spike protein of the coronavirus (SARS-CoV-2). This protein helps the virus to enter human cells. By knowing its 3D structure, scientists identified it as a drug target. Thus, they designed vaccines and medicines that block the spike protein, preventing the virus from infecting more cells.
